name: Old Bess water-returning engine
summary: Old Bess, a large Watt separate-condenser engine at Soho, pumped water back up from the mill's tail race so the waterwheel kept turning.
description: The larger Soho separate-condenser pumping engine known as Old Bess, returning tail-race water to the mill’s head race.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.
why: The Soho mill relied on a waterwheel whose stream could run short, so returning spent water kept the mill supplied.

date.label: by c. 1779
date.basis: The museum identifies the pumping engine as 1777; Watt’s memoir as quoted by Smiles gives a larger replacement about 1778 or 1779.

events.statement: The museum identifies Old Bess as the water-returning mill engine; Watt’s quoted memoir places the larger replacement around 1778–1779.
events.caveats: The museum’s 1777 attribution conflicts with the quoted 1778–1779 replacement chronology; exact commissioning and machine alterations are unresolved.

evidence.supports: Museum identifies the surviving Old Bess engine and its use to pump water back to the Soho head race.
